en: The risks that insurance covers can be put into 3 main groups: risks to people, risks to property, and liability risks (risk of having to pay for damage to others).
why: True. Remember the 3 groups: people, property, liability.

en: Insurance works on the idea of 'one for all, all for one'. People help and support each other.
why: True. Insurance is mutual help: many people support each other.

en: When you plan how to deal with a risk, moving the risk to someone else (risk transfer, for example buying insurance) is a good method, no matter how often accidents happen or how big the loss is.
why: False. You can use a risk map. Risk transfer is usually a good choice only for risks where accidents happen rarely but the loss is big. The statement removed this condition and said 'no matter how often or how big'.
trap: 事故の発生頻度や損害の規模にかかわらず

en: Non-life insurance gives people and companies protection (payment for losses). It removes or reduces the fear of money loss from risks. In this way it helps make the economy and society stable and active.
why: True. Non-life insurance makes the economy stable and active.

en: Non-life insurance helps victims of traffic accidents and victims of natural disasters by paying them money for their losses.
why: True. Non-life insurance helps (relieves) victims with money.

en: Non-life insurance has the role of giving protection (payment for losses). But it does not have the role of reducing losses to society.
why: False. Non-life insurance does not only give protection. It also reduces losses to society, for example by helping to prevent traffic accidents and by disaster prevention and reduction work. The statement changed 'does' to 'does not'.
trap: 社会的損失を低減させる役割は果たしていません

en: Agents (insurance sales people) are the main sellers of non-life insurance. They have a very important role: spreading non-life insurance widely in society.
why: True. Agents are the center of non-life insurance sales.

en: Selling more non-life insurance is important. But agents (insurance sales people) must also strongly understand the social role and public nature of insurance, and always keep high goals (a strong sense of mission).
why: True. Agents must understand the social and public role of insurance.

en: The ways of selling non-life insurance can be put into 3 main groups: sales through an agent, direct sales (by the insurance company itself), and sales through an insurance broker.
why: True. 3 sales types: agent, direct, broker.

topic_en: Risk and insurance / The social role of non-life insurance
en_a: The risks that insurance covers are mainly risks where a loss (a minus) happens, for example from natural disasters or car accidents.
en_i: Non-life insurance gives people and companies protection (payment) in case something bad happens. In this way it plays a big role in society: it makes the economy stable and active, it helps victims of accidents and disasters, and it helps prevent and reduce accidents and damage.
why_a: True. Insurance covers risks that only bring a loss.
why_i: True. Remember the social roles: stable economy, helping victims, preventing and reducing damage.

en: For one person, an accident happens by chance. But if you look at a very large number of cases, you can predict, as a probability, how often accidents happen and how big the losses are for the whole group. Insurance uses this idea, called the 'law of large numbers'.
why: True. Law of large numbers = with many cases, you can predict accidents.

en: In insurance, the premiums paid by policyholders include a part used for claim payments, called the 'pure premium'. The total of pure premiums must be equal to the total of claim payments that the insurance company actually pays. Income and payments must balance across all contracts. This is called the 'principle of balance of income and expenditure'.
why: True. Total pure premiums = total claim payments. This is the principle of balance of income and expenditure.

en: The premium (rate) is made of 2 parts: the 'pure premium (rate)' and the 'loading premium (rate)' (the extra part for costs). The agent's commission (rate) is included in the pure premium (rate).
why: False. The agent's commission is not in the pure premium. It is in the loading premium (the part for costs and profit). The statement swapped the two parts.
trap: 純保険料（率）に含まれています

en: An insurance contract is a contract where the insurance company promises 'to pay a claim payment if an insured accident happens', and the policyholder promises 'to pay a premium in return'.
why: True. Company promises to pay claims; policyholder promises to pay premiums.

en: The policyholder is the person who applies for the insurance contract to the insurance company in their own name, makes the contract, and has the duty to pay the premium. Only an individual person (a natural person) can be a policyholder.
why: False. A company (legal person) can also be a policyholder. It is not limited to individuals. The statement added 'only'.
trap: 個人（自然人）に限られています

en: The insurance period is the period in which the insurance company has the duty to pay a claim payment if an insured accident happens during that period.
why: True. Accident inside the insurance period = company must pay.

en: To make contracts smooth and easy, insurance companies usually prepare contract terms in advance. These terms set the content and conditions of the insurance contract in a standard form. These contract terms are called 'insurance policy conditions' (yakkan).
why: True. Standard contract terms made in advance = insurance policy conditions.

en: Insurance policy conditions have 2 kinds: 'general policy conditions' and 'special clauses' (riders). The general policy conditions are applied before (have priority over) the special clauses.
why: False. Special clauses have priority over the general policy conditions. The statement swapped the order.
trap: 普通保険約款が特約に優先して

en: The general policy conditions describe when claim payments are paid and when they are not paid. But they do not describe the duties of the policyholder and others at the time of the contract or after the contract.
why: False. The general policy conditions also describe the duties of the policyholder and others at the time of the contract and after it. The statement changed 'are described' to 'are not described'.
trap: 義務は記載されていません

en: When the contract is made, the policyholder or the insured must correctly tell the insurance company the important facts about the risk that the company asks about (items to disclose). This is called the 'duty of disclosure'.
why: True. Duty of disclosure = tell the facts correctly when making the contract.

en_a: In insurance, many people put money together to make a large shared fund (a money pool). If something bad happens, like an accident or disaster, a large amount of money is paid from the pool to cover the loss.
en_i: In a non-life insurance contract, the insured is the person who may suffer a money loss if an insured accident happens. If a loss happens from an insured accident, the insured has the right to receive the claim payment. The insured also has the duty to pay the premium when the contract is made.
why_a: True. Insurance = many people make a money pool and pay losses from it.
why_i: False. The duty to pay the premium belongs to the policyholder, not the insured. The statement changed the person.
trap_i: 保険料の支払義務を負います

en: Among the items the company asked about at the time of the contract, there are items the insurance company chooses (items to notify). If one of these items changes after the contract is made, the policyholder or the insured must tell the insurance company without delay. This is called the 'duty of notification'.
why: True. Duty of notification = tell the company quickly about changes after the contract.

en: The insurance company pays a claim payment when certain events happen. In return, the policyholder or the insured has the duty to pay the premium.
why: False. Only the policyholder has the duty to pay the premium. The insured does not. The statement added 'or the insured'.

en: If the policyholder or the insured did not disclose correctly on purpose (intention) when making the contract, the insurance company can cancel the contract. But if they did not disclose correctly because of gross negligence (a serious mistake), the insurance company cannot cancel the contract.
why: False. The company can cancel the contract not only for intention, but also for gross negligence. The statement made a fake exception for gross negligence.
trap: 契約を解除することはできません

en: If the insurance company cancels the contract because the policyholder or others broke the 'duty of notification', claim payments are always paid for losses that happened before the cancellation.
why: False. If the company cancels the contract because of a breach of the duty of notification, as a rule, claim payments are not paid, even for losses before the cancellation. The statement used 'always' and flipped the result.

en: If, after the contract is made, the risk for the insured object becomes much smaller, the policyholder can ask the insurance company to return part of the premium for the remaining period, matching the smaller risk.
why: True. Risk goes down a lot = policyholder can ask for a premium refund for the remaining period.

en_a: Insurable interest is the money value (economic interest) that the insured may lose if an insured accident happens.
en_i: Insurable value is 'the value of the insured object'. In a non-life insurance contract, the insurable value is the maximum amount of claim payment the insurance company pays.
why_a: True. Insurable interest = the economic interest the insured may lose.
why_i: True. Insurable value = value of the object = the highest limit of claim payment.

en_a: The policyholder or the insured has a duty of disclosure when making the insurance contract. But even if they break this duty on purpose or by gross negligence, the insurance contract is never cancelled.
en_i: If the policyholder or the insured fails to do the duty of notification on purpose or by gross negligence, the insurance company can cancel the insurance contract.
why_a: False. If the policyholder or the insured does not tell the facts, or tells false facts, on purpose or by gross negligence, the insurance company can cancel the contract. The statement changed 'can be cancelled' to 'is never cancelled'.
why_i: True. Breaking the duty of notification on purpose or by gross negligence = the company can cancel.
trap_a: 保険契約が解除されることはありません

en: Compulsory automobile liability insurance (CALI, jibaiseki) has the goal of protecting victims whose life or body was harmed by the use of a car. So it covers only accidents that injure or kill people (personal injury accidents).
why: True. CALI covers only injury and death of people, not damage to things.

en: For CALI claim payments, there is a maximum amount per victim. The maximum depends on the kind of loss, such as death, permanent disability (after-effects), or injury.
why: True. CALI has limits per victim: death, permanent disability, injury.

en: The Automobile Liability Security Act (Jibaiho) says that the government runs an Automobile Accident Compensation Guarantee Program, separate from CALI. It helps victims of hit-and-run accidents and victims hit by cars that have no CALI.
why: True. Hit-and-run or no-CALI car = the government program helps the victim.

en: Bodily injury liability insurance in voluntary auto insurance is for when you kill or injure another person in a car accident. It pays the part of the loss that is more than the CALI payment.
why: True. Voluntary bodily injury liability pays the amount above CALI.

en: Personal injury protection (jinshin shogai) in voluntary auto insurance is for when the insured is killed or injured in a car accident while riding in the insured car. It pays for the actual loss, up to the insured amount. It pays whether there is another party or it is a single-car accident, and no matter what the insured's share of fault is.
why: True. Personal injury protection pays the actual loss regardless of fault share.

en: Vehicle (car damage) insurance in voluntary auto insurance is for damage to the insured car from a crash or contact with another car. It pays nothing at all for damage from typhoons, floods, and similar events.
why: False. Vehicle insurance covers damage to the insured car from accidental events. It also pays for damage from typhoons and floods. The statement used 'nothing at all'.

en: Fire insurance covers damage to buildings and household goods not only from fire, lightning, and bursting/explosion, but also from wind damage (storms) and water damage (floods).
why: True. Fire insurance also covers wind and flood damage.

en_a: CALI is insurance for protecting victims of car accidents. Under the Automobile Liability Security Act, as a rule, all cars, including motorized bicycles (mopeds), must have it.
en_i: In bodily injury liability insurance in voluntary auto insurance, if the insured causes an accident that injures a person while driving the insured car after drinking alcohol, no claim payment is paid.
why_a: True. CALI is required for all cars, including mopeds.
why_i: False. Bodily injury liability insurance pays even for accidents from driving without a license or after drinking. This is to protect (help) the victim. The statement changed 'paid' to 'not paid'.
trap_i: 保険金は支払われません

en: Fire insurance covers only the damage to buildings and household goods from fire and similar events. It does not cover costs that come with that damage, such as cleaning up after the fire or apologizing to neighbors.
why: False. Fire insurance also pays for certain costs that come with the damage, like cleaning up after the fire and apologizing to neighbors. The statement added 'only'.

en: When making a fire insurance contract, you must correctly estimate the value of the insured object. You must set a suitable insured amount for the building and for the household goods separately.
why: True. Set the right insured amount for building and household goods separately.

en: Earthquake insurance is based on the Act on Earthquake Insurance. Its goal is to help the lives of disaster victims become stable. The government and non-life insurance companies run it together, so it is very public in nature.
why: True. Earthquake insurance = run by the government and insurance companies together.

en: Earthquake insurance must be added (set) to a fire insurance contract. Its insured amount is the same as the insured amount of the main fire insurance contract.
why: False. The insured amount of earthquake insurance is set separately from the fire insurance. It is 30% to 50% of the main fire insurance amount, with a maximum of 50 million yen for a building and 10 million yen for household goods. The statement said 'the same amount'.

en: In earthquake insurance, if a building or household goods are damaged by an earthquake or similar event, the claim payment depends on the level of damage: 'total loss', 'large half loss', 'small half loss', or 'partial loss'.
why: True. Remember the 4 levels: total, large half, small half, partial.

en_a: Fire insurance does not pay claim payments (except the earthquake fire expense payment) for damage caused by intention or gross negligence of the policyholder or insured, by breaking the law, or by earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, or tsunamis caused by them.
en_i: Earthquake insurance pays for damage that happens within 30 days, counting from the day after the earthquake, volcanic eruption, or tsunami caused by them.
why_a: True. Fire insurance does not cover earthquake damage (except the earthquake fire expense payment).
why_i: False. Damage that happens after 10 days have passed (counting from the day after the earthquake, eruption, or tsunami) is not paid. The statement changed 10 days to 30 days.

en: Personal accident insurance pays claim payments when the insured is injured by a 'sudden, accidental, and external accident', and as a result goes to hospital (stays in or visits), dies, or gets a permanent disability (after-effect).
why: True. Remember the 3 conditions: sudden, accidental, external.

en: The claim payments in personal accident insurance include: death benefit, permanent disability benefit, hospital stay benefit, surgery benefit, and hospital visit (outpatient) benefit.
why: True. 5 kinds: death, permanent disability, hospital stay, surgery, hospital visit.

en: Medical insurance is for money risks that public health insurance does not cover. It pays claim payments only when the insured stays in or visits a hospital because of illness.
why: False. Medical insurance pays not only for illness, but also when the insured stays in or visits a hospital because of injury. The statement added 'only'.
